    // The summed boundary length of the components (holes included).
    Perimeter(s: PolygonSet2D): Number
        => SumOf(s.Polygons.Map(p => p.Perimeter));

    // The union of the component bounds. Precondition: at least one component (the
    // declaration allows an empty set, for which there is no bounding rectangle).
    Bounds(s: PolygonSet2D): Bounds2D
        => s.Polygons.Map(p => p.Bounds)
            .Reduce(s.Polygons.First.Bounds, (acc, b) => UnionOfBounds(acc, b));

    // Inside any component.
    Contains(s: PolygonSet2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => s.Polygons.Any(p => p.Contains(point));

    // The set with every component carried through the mapping.
    Deform(s: PolygonSet2D, mapping: Function1<Point2D, Point2D>): PolygonSet2D
        => PolygonSet2D(s.Polygons.Map(p => p.Deform(mapping)));

    //==
    // # RegularStar2D
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_polygon

    // The 2 * PointCount vertices in ring order, alternating outer and inner,
    // counter-clockwise from Rotation. Even indices are tips.
    RegularStarVertices(s: RegularStar2D): Array<Point2D>
        => (s.PointCount * 2).MapRange(i =>
        {
            var radius = i.IsEven ? s.OuterRadius : s.InnerRadius;
            var a = s.Rotation + (i.ToNumber / (2.0 * s.PointCount.ToNumber)).Turns;
            return s.Center + Vector2D(a.Cos, a.Sin) * radius;
        });

    // n * R * r * sin(pi/n): the star is 2n triangles from the centre, each with
    // sides R and r meeting at pi/n, so each has area (1/2)*R*r*sin(pi/n).
    Area(s: RegularStar2D): Number
        => s.PointCount.ToNumber * s.OuterRadius * s.InnerRadius
        * (0.5 / s.PointCount.ToNumber).Turns.Sin;

    // 2n equal edges, each the third side of a triangle with sides R and r meeting
    // at pi/n: sqrt(R^2 + r^2 - 2*R*r*cos(pi/n)) by the law of cosines.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_cosines
    Perimeter(s: RegularStar2D): Number
        => 2.0 * s.PointCount.ToNumber
        * (s.OuterRadius.Square + s.InnerRadius.Square
            - 2.0 * s.OuterRadius * s.InnerRadius
                * (0.5 / s.PointCount.ToNumber).Turns.Cos).Sqrt;


    // TIGHT: the bounds of the computed vertices (only the tips can be extreme).
    Bounds(s: RegularStar2D): Bounds2D
        => s.RegularStarVertices.BoundsOfPoints;

    // Even-odd containment over the computed vertex ring. The star is non-convex,
    // which the even-odd rule handles correctly.
    Contains(s: RegularStar2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => s.RegularStarVertices.PolygonContainsPoint(point);

    //==
    // # Planar-polygon kernels in space
    //
    // The SPACE analogues of the 2D ring kernels in `geometry.library.plato`:
    // Newell's vector area, a stable in-plane projection basis, the projected even-odd
    // containment test, the fan-decomposition centroid of a planar ring, and the bodily
    // translation of a box. Every polygon body that works in 3D is written in terms of
    // these, and `TranslateBounds` additionally serves the swept-solid bounds in
    // `spatial-primitives.library.plato`.

    //==
    // # Planar-polygon kernels in space

    // The vector area of a closed ring: (1/2) * sum of Pi x Pi+1 over the position
    // vectors. Its magnitude is the enclosed area and its direction is the
    // right-hand-rule normal, both independent of where the origin sits (the
    // origin-dependent terms cancel around a closed loop). Newell's method.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon#Area
    VectorArea(points: Array<Point3D>): Vector3D
        => points.Count
            .MapRange(i => points[i].PositionVector.Cross(points.AtModulo(i + 1).PositionVector))
            .Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (acc, c) => acc + c)
            * 0.5;

    // Any unit vector perpendicular to `normal`. Crossed against whichever world
    // axis `normal` is least aligned with, so the construction never degenerates;
    // the resulting azimuth is arbitrary but stable, which is all a projection
    // basis needs. Precondition: normal is non-zero.
    PlaneTangent(normal: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => (normal.Z.Abs < 0.9 ? Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0) : Vector3D(1.0, 0.0, 0.0))
            .Cross(normal).Normalize;

    // A space point expressed in the plane coordinates (u, v) anchored at `origin`.
    PlaneCoordinates(origin: Point3D, u: Vector3D, v: Vector3D, p: Point3D): Point2D
        => (origin.Between(p).Dot(u), origin.Between(p).Dot(v));

    // True when `point` projects INSIDE the planar ring. Only the in-plane position
    // is tested: a point far off the plane whose projection lands inside reports
    // true, so callers must check the plane distance themselves when they care.
    // Exact for any simple planar polygon, convex or not.
    PlanarPolygonContains(points: Array<Point3D>, normal: Vector3D, point: Point3D): Boolean
    {
        var u = PlaneTangent(normal);
        var v = normal.Normalize.Cross(u);
        var origin = points.First;
        var flat = points.Map(q => PlaneCoordinates(origin, u, v, q));
        return flat.PolygonContainsPoint(PlaneCoordinates(origin, u, v, point));
    }

    // The area centroid of a planar ring in space: the area-weighted mean of the
    // fan triangles (P0, Pi, Pi+1), each weighted by its SIGNED area about the
    // polygon normal. The signs make the fan exact for a non-convex simple polygon
    // too — the triangles that stray outside the ring cancel.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centroid#By_geometric_decomposition
    // Precondition: non-zero area.
    PlanarPolygonCentroid(points: Array<Point3D>): Point3D
    {
        var normal = points.VectorArea.Normalize;
        var origin = points.First;
        var count = points.Count;
        var areas = count.MapRange(i => 0.5 * origin.Between(points[i])
            .Cross(origin.Between(points.AtModulo(i + 1))).Dot(normal));
        var total = SumOf(areas);
        var cx = SumOf(count.MapRange(i => areas[i]
            * (origin.X + points[i].X + points.AtModulo(i + 1).X) / 3.0));
        var cy = SumOf(count.MapRange(i => areas[i]
            * (origin.Y + points[i].Y + points.AtModulo(i + 1).Y) / 3.0));
        var cz = SumOf(count.MapRange(i => areas[i]
            * (origin.Z + points[i].Z + points.AtModulo(i + 1).Z) / 3.0));
        return (cx / total, cy / total, cz / total);
    }

    // The bounds translated bodily by `offset`.
    TranslateBounds(b: Bounds3D, offset: Vector3D): Bounds3D
        => (b.Min + offset, b.Max + offset);

    //==
    // # Polyline length and deformation
    //
    // The length and deformation bodies for the chains declared in
    // `polygons.types.plato`. The `Closed` flag decides whether the wrap-around edge
    // counts; the underlying `ChainLength` kernel is in `geometry.library.plato`.

    //==
    // # Polylines

    // The summed length of the chain; the wrap-around edge counts only when Closed.
    Length(p: Polyline2D): Number
        => p.Points.ChainLength(p.Closed);

    // The summed length of the chain in space.
    Length(p: Polyline3D): Number
        => p.Points.ChainLength(p.Closed);

    // The summed length of the chain in N dimensions. Written out rather than
    // delegated because ChainLength is spelled for Point2D/Point3D only; PointN's
    // delta type is VectorN, whose Magnitude comes from INormed.
    Length(p: PolylineN): Number
        => SumOf((p.Closed ? p.Points.Count : p.Points.Count - 1)
            .MapRange(i => p.Points[i].Between(p.Points.AtModulo(i + 1)).Magnitude));
